newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa SAA faces heavy losses in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa SAA faces heavy losses in 1996/97.

text.p: State-run South African Airways will show an unaudited loss of 345 million rand for the financial year ended March 1997 but has budgeted to break even during the current year, Business Day newspaper said on Monday.
An SAA spokeswoman confirmed to Reuters that the airline expected a substantial loss in 1996/97 but was unable to say the exact figure.
The paper said the big losses were attributable to an increase in operating costs. At the same time unrest among technical workers last year cost the flag carrier 60 million rand.
Fuel prices were 130 million more than budgeted due to the fall in the rand and yields from international services were also low, reflecting increased competition on the South African route.

However, chief executive Mike Myburgh expects to break even this year by revamping operations, including introducing profitable new destinations such as Japan and Denmark, and increasing the frequency of flights to lucrative destinations such as the U.S., Europe and the Far East.
Loss-making destinations such as Munich, Dusseldorf and Rio de Janeiro would be axed, the paper said.
Third-party technical maintenance contracts would also be extra money-spinners -- already contracts worth about 30 million had been concluded recently.
SAA is one of several state enterprises that the government plans to privatise, initially via the introduction of a strategic equity partner.
